subject: Unity-chan (Kohaku Otori) as a Terran-style infantry unit
gunModel: Quaternius Ultimate Guns Pack AssaultRifle2_1.fbx (CC0 1.0), 0.92 m, restyled materials + edge bevel
renderer: Eevee, 16 samples, Standard view transform, transparent film, pixel filter 1.0, anisotropic texture filter 16x; rendered at 2x the HD canvas (1280 px) and reduced by 2 (supersample.py: premultiplied Lanczos for colour/albedo, premultiplied box for mask, shadow and data layers)

camera.scaleChoice: 2.5x 64 px/m (user 2026-11-09); the native Goliath (unit 3 base image 234 + turret image 235, HD frame 16 south) is 227 HD px tall, matched at about 159 px/m

light.key: sun from the screen upper left (azimuth 135 deg = world -X,+Y), elevation 50 deg
light.rim: sun from behind on the upper left (azimuth 115 deg, elevation 28 deg), energy 2.6 (key 3.2)
light.shadowProjection: planar onto the ground along azimuth 135 deg, elevation 70 deg

scale.sd: HD downscaled by 4 with a premultiplied box filter

directions.mirrored: facings 17..31 = horizontal flip of facings 15..1; frames are symmetric about the pivot x

files.pivotNote: pivot = ground point under the feet, as the pixel-corner offset from the top-left; colour, mask and shadow share frame size and pivot

layers.emissive: hd/{animation}/d{direction:02}_f{frame:02}_emissive.png (only frames in emissiveFrames; other frames = transparent black)
layers.note: HD only, same frame size and pivot as the colour frame; 'diffuse' = the existing colour frame, 'teamcolor' = the existing _mask frame. SD stays diffuse + mask (the SD path has no lighting).

teamColor: masked objects: blue sleeves (shirts_sode, shirts_sode_BK), headband (hairband), hair accessories (hair_accce); original colours kept in the colour image

walk.gun: low-ready (IK hands on the gun), legs from the clip, in place

attack.clip: WAIT00 frame 10 legs + authored arm IK pose
attack.gun: raise 18 deg down, aim level, recoil 4 deg up and 3 cm back; frame 2 = frame 1 + muzzle flash

death.gun: in the right hand for frames 0-4, lying on the ground from frame 5; collapse only, no blood or gore
death.note: hips travel halved so the body stays centred on the unit position

lightingLayers.source: scr-render HdImageLoader (layer selection), HdSceneRenderer (deferred sprite shader), HdLighting (resolve shader), scr-data AnimFile (layer table)
lightingLayers.litPathRule: the lit pass draws 'bright' instead of 'diffuse' and uses the frame's lighting only when bright, normal, specular and ao_depth all exist (and frame flag 8 is clear); otherwise it draws diffuse with flat default layers
lightingLayers.shipAsDiffuse: the existing colour frame (baked lighting) as 'diffuse' for the unlit path; the _bright frame (albedo, no baked lighting) as 'bright' for the lit path
lightingLayers.bright: RGBA, unlit base colour (albedo) as sRGB bytes like the colour frame, used as-is by the shader; alpha = the colour frame's alpha (the G-buffer coverage); muzzle flash pixels black
lightingLayers.normal: R = x, A = y (each n * 0.5 + 0.5); the shader reads only R and A and rebuilds z = sqrt(max(1 - x^2 - y^2, 0.1)); +x = screen right, +y = screen up, +z = towards the viewer; mirrored facings: the renderer negates x. G = y and B = z are copies for viewing (the converter clears them: native frames keep G and B black). E12l: the baked normal's tilt is blended with the viewer direction by normalStrength (soft, native-like lambert). Outside the silhouette (128,128,255,128) = the renderer's flat default
lightingLayers.specular: RGB = specular colour added as pow(dot(N, H), 16) * rgb (Blinn-Phong, times AO); grey (0.08 + 0.85 * metallic) * (1 - roughness) * 1.2: rifle metal 0.43-0.57, polymer 0.04, skin/cloth 0.014, hair 0.04, eyes 0.08; E12l: at least specularFloor (41, the native Marine's lowest byte); A = 255 (unused); outside (0,0,0,255) = default
lightingLayers.ao_depth: G = ambient occlusion (multiplies the lit colour), A = depth: fragment z = A * 75 * lightingScale HD pixels for point lights (lights sit at z 125); baked as 0.06 + how far the surface stands out towards the viewer from the unit's ground point (world -Y) in HD pixels / 75 (160 px/m), clamped to 0..1, then (E12l) 0.06 + (value - 0.06) * depthFactor (native Goliath range); calibrated against the native Marine (main_239.anim ao_depth alpha about 0.1 at the feet, 0.2 on the torso); R and B unused (AO copied); outside (255,255,255,0) = default
lightingLayers.emissive: RGB added after lighting and written to the bloom input (pixels over luminance 1.8 bloom); only the muzzle flash (1.0, 0.75, 0.3) in emissiveFrames; A = 255 where lit, unused
lightingLayers.aoMethod: Eevee Ambient Occlusion shader node, distance 0.30 m
lightingLayers.resolution: every layer at the HD frame size (renderer samples all layers with the diffuse texture coordinates, so a layer texture only needs the same atlas layout)

portrait.source: scr-client PortraitPlayer/PortraitTables/PortraitStatic, scr-data PortraitTypeTable; native TMarine clips probed read-only
portrait.nativeLayout: clip path = <set prefix><portdata.tbl directory string><n>.webm; set prefix SD/portrait/, HD2/portrait/, portrait/ (HD skins: <skin>/portrait/); idle clips n = 0..3 chosen with the portdata.dat idle weights (native 85/5/5/5 %), talking clips n = 0..2 at random (no direct repeat); missing numbers fall back to lower ones; the clip is stretched into the 60x56 portrait control
portrait.nativeFormat: WebM, VP9 profile 1, gbrp (RGB 4:4:4), 10 fps, opaque (no alpha); SD 60x56, HD2 224x240, HD 448x480; Marine clips 10 frames (Fid03 15/16)
portrait.addedUnitNote: an added unit can name its own portrait: a portdata.dat entry (idle and talking directory string ids + 4 idle weights) whose strings point to these clips in the mod's files; today SC:R Crossover reuses the Medic portrait

Fid00.content: breathing nod, one blink (the common idle clip)

Fid01.content: glance to her left and back, blink

Fid03.content: tilt to the other side, double blink

Tlk00.content: talking: mouth A/I/O/E/U blend shapes, closed frames between

files.clips: portrait/{set}/{clip}.webm (VP9 yuv420p from Blender's FFmpeg, 10 fps; re-encode to the native gbrp profile 1 from the PNG frames if needed)

portrait.render: Eevee 32 samples, perspective head-and-shoulders camera on her left (she looks towards the screen left), warm key from the upper left, blue rim from the right back, dark warm-to-navy backdrop; pose WAIT00 frame 10, neck/head rotated per frame, facial blend shapes (EYE_DEF_C blink, MTH_A/I/U/E/O, MTH/EYE/BLW_SMILE1); HD rendered at 448x480, HD2 = HD Lanczos /2, SD rendered at 480x448 (own framing for the wider SD aspect) and Lanczos-reduced to 60x56
portrait.expressions: neutral and friendly only (soft smile); no other expression shapes used

wireframe.source: scr-client ConsoleView.drawWireframe/drawUnitBox and Wireframe (cell entries), scr-render InterfaceAssets (twire.pcx colours); native sheets probed read-only
wireframe.nativeLayout: one .dds.grp frame per unit type: a horizontal strip of square cells, cell size = frame height; each drawn cell is a white mask tinted with its twire.pcx colour and drawn over the same box; cells 0..3 = damage parts (entry from the unit's hit points and randomizer), 4..5 = shield outlines (SD: drawn black when the unit has no shields; HD: skipped), the drawing uses min(6, cells) cells
wireframe.nativeSizes: SD wirefram 384x64 (6 cells of 64, DXT1, 1-bit white), SD grpwire/tranwire 192x32 (6 cells of 32); HD2 wirefram 1024x128 and HD 2048x256 (8 cells: 4 parts, 2 shield outlines, the whole picture, one empty; DXT5 soft white lines); HD/HD2 group and transport views draw the main HD strip into the 32x32 box (HD grpwire/tranwire are single cropped pictures, not read by the current drawing)
wireframe.partMethod: vertex part = part of its strongest bone (Head/Neck/Hair/Ribbon -> 0, Hips/legs/skirt -> 2, other bones -> 1, rifle -> 3); lines = silhouette, part borders, creases over 52 deg and depth steps over 4.8 cm on the 1024 px render, put on the nearer pixel's part
wireframe.pose: WAIT00 frame 10 with the rifle at low-ready, facing index 19 (towards the screen left), orthographic, 12 deg down

commandIcon.source: scr-client ConsoleView.drawCommandIconShifted, scr-render InterfaceAssets; native cmdicons probed
commandIcon.nativeFormat: unit/cmdicons/cmdicons.dds.grp, one frame per icon: SD 32x32, HD2 64x64, HD 128x128, DXT1 (1-bit alpha), grey (the state tint is applied when drawn); SD centring uses the classic cmdicons.grp frame width/height (give visibleSize)
commandIcon.render: attack aim pose, facing index 21, orthographic 22 deg down, Eevee; grey = luminance with levels matched to the native Marine/Ghost icons (HD 5/50/95 % = 6/50/215, SD 8/41/120); alpha >= 128 -> opaque

formatChanges0.2: E12h: ao_depth depth calibrated to the native Marine, new parts portrait, wireframe, commandIcon; E12i: 160 px/m (canvasHd 640), 2x supersampled renders, rim light (values only, same structure)
formatChanges0.3: 'quality' names the quality of the baked frames (folder and frameSize/pivot key: hd or hd2); attack frames that hit are listed in 'actionFrames' (before: the emissive frames)
